label: Number Theory
shortDescription: The queen of mathematics. From elementary divisibility and primes to analytic and algebraic number theory.
modulesDescription: Read the number-theory chapters in order, or jump directly to the topic you need.
ogTitle: Learn Number Theory for Free | CalcPath
ogDescription: Master number theory from divisors and primes through quadratic residues, Diophantine equations, the prime number theorem, and algebraic number theory — with rich explanations and hundreds of practice problems.
courseDescription: A free in-depth course on number theory: elementary topics (divisibility, primes, Euclidean algorithm, modular arithmetic, Fermat and Wilson theorems), arithmetic functions and convolutions, quadratic reciprocity and Gauss sums, classical Diophantine equations including Pell and Pythagorean triples, analytic number theory (zeta, PNT, Dirichlet theorems), and algebraic number theory (algebraic integers, rings of integers, Dedekind domains, class groups, units). Every topic includes ELI5 intuitions, detailed worked examples, common mistakes, and targeted practice questions.

topics.title: Divisors & Primes
topics.description: Divisibility and its algebra; the division algorithm with existence and uniqueness; tau and sigma from the factorisation, with odd tau characterising the squares; Euclid's infinitude of primes and a second proof via Fermat numbers; the sieve proved correct and the sqrt(n) bound; the Euclidean algorithm, Bezout, Euclid's lemma, and the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic with existence and uniqueness kept separate; and Lame's bound with its Fibonacci worst case.

topics.title: Modular Arithmetic
topics.description: Congruence as an equivalence relation compatible with the arithmetic; Z/nZ as a ring, a field exactly for prime n; inverses via the extended Euclidean algorithm and the full linear-congruence theorem; fast modular exponentiation; the Chinese Remainder Theorem with its explicit formula and the non-coprime case; quadratic residues, Euler's criterion, the Legendre symbol and when -1 is a square; and the Jacobi symbol with Solovay-Strassen.

topics.title: Classical Theorems
topics.description: Fermat's little theorem proved twice, by rearranging residues and via Lagrange; Euler's generalisation; Wilson's theorem in both directions; why the Fermat primality test fails, with Korselt's criterion and 561 worked; and quadratic reciprocity proved in full through Gauss's lemma and Eisenstein's lattice-point count, with both supplementary laws.

topics.title: Arithmetic Functions
topics.description: Dirichlet convolution and the ring it makes, with multiplicativity preserved under convolution as the engine of the chapter; Euler's totient derived three ways; the Mobius function, the key identity, and inversion in both directions as a convolution statement; sigma_k and the Euclid-Euler characterisation of even perfect numbers; the Carmichael function and Korselt's criterion; and Mertens' theorems.

topics.title: Diophantine Equations
topics.description: Linear equations solvable exactly when the gcd divides the constant, with the full solution set; primitive Pythagorean triples parametrised in both directions, and again through the Gaussian integers; Pell's equation, its fundamental solution and the group structure of all solutions; the Hasse-Minkowski local-global principle and Selmer's cubic counterexample; and Fermat's Last Theorem for n=4 proved completely by infinite descent.

topics.title: Analytic Number Theory
topics.description: The zeta function, its convergence, and the Euler product derived from unique factorisation; the pole at s=1 and Euler's proof that the reciprocals of the primes diverge; Chebyshev's elementary bounds and Mertens' estimate; the prime number theorem with its equivalents; Dirichlet characters, their orthogonality, and L-functions; Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions reduced to one non-vanishing statement; and the Riemann hypothesis stated precisely.

topics.title: Algebraic Number Theory
topics.description: Algebraic integers and the integrality criterion; the ring of integers, computed explicitly for quadratic fields including the d = 1 mod 4 case; the failure of unique factorisation in Z[sqrt(-5)] and its restoration at the level of ideals in a Dedekind domain; the ideal class group, with class number one exactly when the ring of integers is a UFD; and Dirichlet's unit theorem with the rank formula worked for quadratic, cubic and cyclotomic fields.
